issues.t: Head gasket failure or slipped cylinder liner
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, the engine runs hot, white smoke or a sweet smell comes from the exhaust, or a ticking noise appears once the engine is warm.
issues.why: The aluminum Rover V8 used in these years is known for head gasket leaks, and on some engines a cylinder liner can shift in the block (a 'slipped liner'). Both let coolant escape and combustion gas into the cooling system.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Ask a shop for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test. A head gasket job is costly but fixable; a slipped liner usually means a rebuilt or replacement engine, so get a firm diagnosis before spending money.

issues.t: Main bearing failure and low oil pressure
issues.sym: The oil pressure light flickers or stays on, and a deep knocking noise comes from the bottom of the engine.
issues.why: Owners of late Series I Discoveries report crankshaft main bearings wearing out, which lets oil pressure fall and can destroy the engine.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the oil light comes on. Check the oil level, then have oil pressure measured with a gauge before driving further. Bearing damage usually means an engine rebuild.

issues.t: Oil pump failure
issues.sym: Oil pressure warning light, low oil pressure on the gauge, or new engine noise.
issues.why: Several owners of the 4.6L V8 report oil pump failures between about 65,000 and 106,000 miles.
issues.next: Stop the engine if the oil pressure light comes on and do not drive until oil pressure is tested. Catching it early can save the engine.

issues.t: Overheating from clogged radiator or failed water pump
issues.sym: Temperature gauge rises in traffic or hot weather, coolant smell, or coolant dripping at the front of the engine.
issues.why: Radiators on the Discovery II clog internally with age, and water pumps leak or fail. Overheating is especially harmful to these V8s because it can lead to head gasket and liner failure.
issues.next: Do not keep driving an overheating engine. Have the radiator flow and water pump checked. Replacing a clogged radiator early is much cheaper than an engine repair.

issues.t: ABS, traction control and hill descent lights all on
issues.sym: The ABS, traction control and hill descent control warning lights come on together (owners call them the 'three amigos'). ABS may stop working.
issues.why: A fault in the ABS system, often a wheel speed sensor, wiring or the ABS control unit, turns off ABS, traction control and hill descent control at the same time.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but ABS may not. Have the ABS codes read with a scan tool; a single wheel sensor is a cheap fix, while a control unit costs more.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve covers and oil pan
issues.sym: Oil spots under the SUV, burning oil smell after a drive, or oily residue on the engine and exhaust.
issues.why: Valve cover and oil pan gaskets on these V8s harden and leak with age.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and top up. Have the leak traced; gaskets are inexpensive, but oil dripping on the exhaust can be a fire risk.

issues.t: Driveshaft vibration from worn U-joints or rear coupling
issues.sym: Vibration that builds with speed, a clunk when shifting into gear, or a knock under the SUV.
issues.why: Front driveshaft universal joints wear out, and the rubber flexible coupling on the rear driveshaft cracks with age.
issues.next: Have the driveshafts checked for play. A failed coupling can let the driveshaft drop, so do not ignore new vibration.

issues.t: Cruise control wire can set off driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning. A chafed wire can overheat the steering wheel connector and fire the driver airbag unexpectedly.
issues.why: A cruise control wire in the steering wheel can chafe and short.
issues.next: Have a Land Rover dealer check with your VIN that the fusible link from this recall was installed. The fix is free.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor failure
issues.sym: A suspension fault message, the SUV stuck low or only 'normal height' available, or the compressor running loudly or for a long time.
issues.why: The air suspension compressor wears out, often after years of working to make up for small leaks. It is one of the most common LR3 and LR4 repairs.
issues.next: Have the air suspension scanned for codes and leaks. Fix any leaks at the same time as the compressor, or the new compressor will wear out early.

issues.t: Air strut leak or height sensor fault
issues.sym: One corner sits lower after parking, the SUV leans, a suspension fault warning appears, or the suspension drops to its lowest setting.
issues.why: Rubber air springs crack and leak with age, and ride height sensors fail. A bad height sensor can switch the air suspension off.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks and sensor faults with a scan tool. Driving a long way on a deflated corner can damage tires and other suspension parts.

issues.t: Wheel bearing or hub failure
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed, play in a wheel, or an ABS light.
issues.why: Wheel bearings are the single most reported LR3 repair, and LR4s also see failures. The heavy SUV wears them out.
issues.next: Have the wheel checked for play. Replace a noisy bearing soon, since a badly worn bearing can damage the hub and ABS sensor.

issues.t: Worn control arm bushings and ball joints
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a shimmy or shake under hard braking, wandering steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The lower control arm bushings and ball joints wear out under the heavy SUV. Owners note that cheap aftermarket arms can fail quickly.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked for worn bushings. Use good-quality parts and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Thermostat housing cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Low coolant warning, coolant puddle or crust near the front of the engine, or a sweet smell.
issues.why: The plastic thermostat housing on the LR3 cracks with heat cycles. It is one of the most repeated LR3 repairs.
issues.next: Keep coolant topped up and have the housing replaced before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant leak at the front of the engine, low coolant warning, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: Water pumps on the LR3 and LR4 V8 engines commonly start leaking around 60,000-120,000 miles.
issues.next: Replace a leaking pump promptly; overheating can ruin the engine. Replace the thermostat at the same time if it is due.

issues.t: Coolant leak from plastic crossover pipes
issues.sym: Coolant keeps dropping with no obvious leak, coolant smell, or coolant pooling in the engine valley.
issues.why: The 5.0L V8 uses plastic coolant pipes between the cylinder heads that crack, and small leaks are hard to find. Upgraded pipes are available.
issues.next: Have a pressure test done. Ask for the upgraded crossover pipes, often fitted at the same time as the water pump.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake sticks or fails
issues.sym: Parking brake warning light, the parking brake won't release or won't apply, or grinding from the rear brakes.
issues.why: The electric parking brake actuator and its small brake shoes inside the rear rotors fail, and the brake can seize on.
issues.next: Do not drive with a dragging parking brake. A shop with a Land Rover scan tool can test the actuator and put the system in service mode.

issues.t: Transmission fault message from rear locker motor
issues.sym: A 'transmission fault' message, sometimes with the air suspension dropping to access height.
issues.why: The small electric motor on the rear locking differential fails and sets codes that show up as a transmission fault.
issues.next: Have the codes read before assuming the gearbox is bad. Replacing the differential motor is a much smaller job.

issues.t: Clogged sunroof drains flood wiring
issues.sym: Wet carpets or headliner, electrical gremlins, warning messages, or the SUV not starting after rain.
issues.why: The sunroof drains clog, and water runs into the cabin where it can soak wiring and control modules.
issues.next: Clean the sunroof drains regularly. If you find water inside, dry it out fast and have the wiring and modules checked.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: Battery or charging warning, dim lights, or a dead battery.
issues.why: Alternators commonly fail on the LR3 and LR4. One LR4 owner found an aftermarket unit did not fix the fault and a genuine part did.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Use a quality original-equipment alternator.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leaks
issues.sym: Red fluid under the SUV, harsh or slipping shifts, or a transmission warning.
issues.why: Leaks at the transmission pan gasket, seals and the electrical connector sleeve are common on the LR3.
issues.next: Check for drips and have the fluid level checked by a shop (there is no dipstick). Fix leaks early; running low can damage the transmission.

issues.t: Battery drains and won't start
issues.sym: Slow cranking, no-start, or a 'start engine to charge battery' warning.
issues.why: LR4 owners report batteries with weak cells and low charge, and the electronics place a heavy load on the battery.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. A new battery may need to be registered with a scan tool.

issues.t: Driver airbag wiring can break (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light comes on.
issues.why: Movement of the steering column cover can break the driver airbag wiring at the clockspring, so the airbag may not fully deploy.
issues.next: Have a Land Rover dealer confirm the spacers and pads from this recall were fitted. The fix is free.

issues.t: Fuel tank outlet flange can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or fuel dripping near the tank.
issues.why: The flange where fuel leaves the tank can crack, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside away from ignition sources and contact a dealer. The flange replacement is free.

issues.t: Rear doors may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door looks closed but can open while driving, and the door-ajar warning may not show.
issues.why: The keyless UniLatch entry system can fail to latch the rear passenger doors.
issues.next: Make sure the rear doors are fully shut and contact a dealer. The free fix disables the UniLatch function.

issues.t: Check engine light from exhaust manifold leak
issues.sym: Check engine light that returns after being cleared, and sometimes a ticking noise when cold.
issues.why: An exhaust leak at the manifold (header) can trigger engine codes. One owner needed several dealer visits before it stayed fixed.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the manifold checked for leaks. Ask the dealer for a repair history if the light keeps returning.

issues.t: Engine can shut off after false low-fuel reading (recall)
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows low fuel incorrectly, and the engine may cut out about 17 miles later.
issues.why: A software error makes the fuel gauge read wrong, and the engine can stop when it thinks the tank is empty.
issues.next: Have a dealer install the free software update.

issues.t: No dashboard sign when auto high beams are on (recall)
issues.sym: The dash does not show when the automatic high beams are active.
issues.why: Instrument cluster software did not display the high-beam status, so the SUV did not meet federal lighting rules.
issues.next: Have a dealer install the free software update.

issues.t: Loose battery ground can cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Random electrical faults, loss of exterior lights, or the SUV shutting down while driving.
issues.why: The battery ground stud can lose contact with the body.
issues.next: Contact a dealer; the ground stud is replaced free.

issues.t: DC/DC converter overload can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Battery or charging warnings, then possible loss of drive power or exterior lights while driving.
issues.why: On mild-hybrid models the DC/DC converter can overload under high electrical demand or fail at start-up because of a software error.
issues.next: Check with a dealer that both related recall updates (26V248 and 26V599) are done. The software fix is free.

issues.t: Rear camera can fill with water (recall)
issues.sym: Blank, foggy or distorted rearview camera image.
issues.why: Water collects around the camera because the tailgate trim lacks drain holes.
issues.next: A dealer will add drain holes and replace the camera if needed, free.

issues.t: Driver airbag clockspring connector can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a crash; the driver airbag may not deploy as designed.
issues.why: Corrosion can build up at the connector on the steering wheel clockspring.
issues.next: Have a dealer apply the free protective gel to the connector.

issues.t: Blocked cam carrier oil channel can leak oil (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leak or burning oil smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: A blocked oil passage in the cam carrier can cause an oil leak, which is a fire risk if oil reaches hot parts.
issues.next: Contact a dealer. The cam carrier is inspected and replaced if needed, free.

issues.t: Oil filter housing can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The oil filter housing can crack and leak oil, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Contact a dealer. The housing, filter and seals are replaced free.

issues.t: 'Traction reduced' warning in low range or off-road mode
issues.sym: A 'Traction Reduced - 2 Wheel Drive Only' message appears when you select low range or an off-road driving mode.
issues.why: Land Rover issued a service bulletin for this warning on 2025 models.
issues.next: Note when the message appears and ask a dealer to apply the bulletin. Avoid tough off-road use until it is fixed.

issues.t: Keyless entry and walk-away locking work only sometimes
issues.sym: The doors don't always unlock when you touch the handle, or the SUV doesn't lock itself when you walk away.
issues.why: Land Rover issued bulletins for intermittent passive entry and for walk-away lock and approach unlock not working because of a software limitation.
issues.next: Use the buttons on the key fob in the meantime and ask a dealer for the software update.
